To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BMP signaling is required in the developing cochlea for patterning the nonsensory regions, the outer sulcus and Kölliker's Organ, and the sensory region, the organ of Cortis, and for specifying the prosensory region, which gives rise to the organ of Cortic.
BMP signaling is necessary and sufficient for patterning of the mammalian cochlear sensory epithelium.

1) BMP signaling is necessary and sufficient for patterning the outer sulcus, 2) BMP signaling is also required for patterning the prosensory region of the developing cochlea, and 3) a gradient of BMP signaling is established in an abneural–prosensory–neural direction in the cochlea
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that pattern the mammalian cochlear duct into the sensory organ of Corti and nonsensory regions.
the development of the mammalian inner ear and specifically the development of the sensory organ of Corti that detects sound.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the development and patterning of the inner ear.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“BMP signaling is necessary for patterning sensory (organ of Corti) and nonsensory regions (Kölliker’s organ and outer sulcus) of the developing mammalian cochlea.”
BMP4 signaling is required for specification and maintenance of the prosensor domain in the cochlea.
BMP signaling is required to specify the prosensory territory of the cochlea, and is also required to specify the nonsensory outer sulcus territory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BMP signaling is important for patterning sensory tissue in the mammal cochlea.
BMP4 signaling is necessary for patterning the sensory and nonsensors regions in the cochlea.
BMP4 is required for patterming the sensory region of the cochlear epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMP signaling is required to specify the prosensory and nonsensory regions in the mammalian inner ear.
a gradient of BMP signaling is necessary to establish the sensory and nonsensitory domains in the developing cochlea.

BMP signaling is required in the mammalian ear to specify the nonsensory outer sulcus domain, which is the boundary between the organ of Cortis on the abneuronal side and the nonsensory Kölliker's Organ on the neural side.
